content.text: This section gives standard templates and practical tools for school operations. They help all Eduversal Partner Schools carry out policies, procedures and practices in the same way. Principals and school leadership teams can use them to meet Indonesian regulations, Cambridge International requirements and CIS/WASC accreditation standards. They also help daily operations run efficiently.
All templates in this section follow these principles:

items: Compliance-Ready: Templates include the elements required by the Indonesian MoE (Ministry of Education), Cambridge and CIS/WASC
EAL-Friendly: Language is clear and easy to understand; bilingual versions are available where appropriate
Contextually Adaptable: Schools may change templates to fit their local context, but they keep the core elements
Evidence-Generating: Templates create records that schools can use in accreditation evidence portfolios
EduNav-Compatible: Templates match EduNav platform fields and reporting structures
content.title: 19.1.1 Template Design Principles

content.text: Templates are grouped by functional area. Each template is cross-referenced to the relevant handbook sections. Schools should keep both digital and physical copies of completed templates, as the records retention requirements in Section 14 set out. The Eduversal Template Repository in EduNav is the central place to find current versions and to submit completed forms.

subsections.title: Strategic Planning and School Improvement Templates

content.text: The following templates support the strategic planning and continuous improvement processes in Section 4. They align with CIS Domain A (Purpose and Direction), WASC Category A (Organization for Student Learning) and Indonesian accreditation requirements.

Purpose: To record the school's 3-5 year strategic direction. It links vision and mission to measurable outcomes that align with the Schoolwide Learner Outcomes (SLOs). Cross-Reference: Section 4.2 (Strategic Planning Framework), Section 1.2 (Vision, Mission, and Core Values). Template Structure: Usage Notes: The Strategic Plan should be reviewed every year, with a full revision every 3-5 years. Schools should keep a version history and record evidence of stakeholder consultation. The plan is the foundation for the annual School Improvement Plans (T-02).
content.title: 19.3.1 Strategic Plan Template (T-01)

content.text: Purpose: To turn strategic priorities into annual improvement actions, with clear success criteria and clear accountability. Cross-Reference: Section 4.2 (Strategic Planning Framework), Section 17 (Quality Assurance and Internal Review). SIP Action Plan Format: Required Elements:
content.title: 19.3.2 School Improvement Plan (SIP) Template (T-02)

items: Link each priority to specific SLOs and strategic plan goals

content.text: Purpose: To find and manage possible conflicts of interest among board members, senior leadership, and staff with procurement or hiring responsibilities. Cross-Reference: Section 1.5 (Conflict of Interest Policy), Section 13.7 (Procurement and Vendor Management). content.text: These templates are critical tools for keeping children safe. All Eduversal Partner Schools must use them consistently. They support the requirements in Section 9 and align with CIS Domain E (Wellbeing) and Indonesian child protection regulations.

Purpose: To give a standard format for reporting safeguarding concerns to the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL). It keeps records consistent and makes sure follow-up is appropriate. Cross-Reference: Section 9.8 (Recognizing and Responding to Concerns), Section 9.10 (Record Keeping and Confidentiality). Form Structure: Part A: Reporter Details
content.title: 19.5.1 Safeguarding Concern/Incident Form (T-08)

items: Reporter Name: [Full name, role, contact details] - Required
Date & Time of Report: [When the form was completed]
Date & Time of Concern: [When the concern was observed or disclosed] - Be specific

content.text: Part B: Child/Student Details

items: Date of Birth/Age: [DOB and current age] - Required

content.text: Part C: Concern Details

items.text: Nature of Concern (select all that apply):

items: Description of Concern: [A factual account of what was seen, heard, or disclosed. Use the child's own words in quotation marks where possible. Record facts only, not opinions or interpretations.]
Context: [Where did this occur? Who was present? Any previous concerns?]
Visible Signs/Injuries: [If applicable, describe location, size, color - do not photograph]
Immediate Actions Taken: [Actions to ensure immediate safety, who was informed]
Child's Wishes: [If disclosed, what does the child want to happen?]

content.text: Part D: DSL Response (DSL Use Only)

items: Risk Assessment Level: [ ] Low [ ] Medium [ ] High [ ] Critical
Actions Taken: [Referrals made, parent contact, external agencies notified, support plans started]

content.text: Critical Reminders:

items: Submit to the DSL on the same day; if there is immediate danger, contact emergency services first
Record facts, not interpretations; when the child discloses, use the child's exact words
Keep strict confidentiality; share only with people who need to know
Do not promise the child that you will keep information secret
Do not investigate - that is the role of the DSL and the authorities
Keep the form as the records retention policy says (see Section 14)

content.text: Purpose: To record concerns that are below the threshold for a formal safeguarding referral. These concerns may still form part of a pattern that needs monitoring. Cross-Reference: Section 9.9 (Low-Level Concerns), Section 9.12 (Allegations Against Staff). Log Fields: Categories of Low-Level Concerns:
content.title: 19.5.2 Low-Level Concern Log (T-09)

items: Boundary issues (e.g., language that is too familiar, too much 1:1 contact)
Professional conduct concerns (e.g., inappropriate comments, social media contact)
Pattern of minor complaints from students/parents
Concerning attitudes or behaviors toward students

content.text: Review Protocol: the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) reviews the log every month to find patterns. The DSL also reviews it every year with the Principal and HR. Retention: employment + 25 years after the person leaves the job, as set out in the consolidated schedule at 14.5. This log is a safeguarding record, not a staff discipline record. There are two reasons for this. Its purpose is to show a pattern over time, and a former student may disclose years later. It is kept in the DSL's secure safeguarding files, separate from HR personnel files. At the annual review, entries that never formed part of a pattern are considered for disposal. Keeping these records must stay justified under UU No. 27/2022.

content.text: Observation Domains and Indicators: this form rates the four sub-domains of Domain 2 (Classroom Observation) in the Section 7.3 appraisal structure. This mapping is CORRECTED and may be used. It replaces a legacy version that assigned the same letter to different domains (A to both Purpose and Governance; B to both Teaching and Assessment; D to both Finance and Risk) and used a WASC "Category E" that does not exist.

CIS letters and titles verified against the CIS Quick Guide to Standards, July 2021, pp.2-11; WASC categories against ACS WASC Focus on Learning, 2019 edition, p.66 — Categories A-D only, with school culture in Category C and the schoolwide action plan as a Chapter V deliverable rather than a category.

Two structural points carried over from the correction: assessment is not a separate CIS domain (it is standards D7-D8 inside Domain D), and there is no CIS "Operational Systems" domain — policy and compliance evidence belongs to B6, premises and technology to G.
